description: BGE-M3 dense embeddings, UINT8-quantized ONNX export, for fully local/offline CPU inference.

source.quantization: uint8 (dynamic quantization of the ONNX export, as published by Xenova)

notes: Copied verbatim (byte-for-byte, sha256-verified) from the local Hugging Face cache at ~/.cache/pka-embed-bench/models/models--Xenova--bge-m3, already fetched during prior offline embedding-model benchmarking (see EMBEDDING_MODEL_BENCHMARK.pdf / eval/BENCHMARK_RESULTS.md). No network download was performed to produce this pinned copy.

Benchmarked against eval/run_benchmark.py's real corpus/queries on 2026-08-25 (see eval/BENCHMARK_RESULTS.md's addendum): identical top-1 accuracy and recall@5 to fp32 BAAI/bge-m3, ~24% faster ingestion, ~37% faster query. Its separability gap is roughly half fp32's (0.011 vs 0.024) — still positive on this small corpus (6 documents, 23 queries), but a thinner margin. Re-measure before lowering RETRIEVAL_MIN_SCORE for this provider.

The .onnx/.json model files alongside this manifest are intentionally untracked by git (see .gitignore) — this manifest is the durable, version-controlled record of provenance; the files themselves are a local pinned cache copy, not a repo asset.

Production must not mix vectors from this model with the existing Ollama-served BAAI/bge-m3 embeddings: use a distinct CHROMA_COLLECTION (ADR-8 enforces this automatically via the embedding fingerprint).
